mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate reduces the cost of capital for corporations, increasing the present value of future earnings and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS is below 5.0%, the S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in the unemployment rate above 4.0% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE > 4.0, the S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such periods, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) signals a broad-based weakening in consumer demand, reducing corporate revenue expectations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When HOUST < 1400.0 and RSAFS < 680000.0, the S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such periods, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During a supply-driven expansion (INDPRO > 102.5), manufacturing output growth supports corporate profit margins, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO > 102.5, the S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the CPI (CPIAUCSL > 305.0) signals persistent inflation, prompting the Fed to maintain restrictive policy, which pressures equity valuations and causes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL > 305.0, the S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such periods, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Strong labor market growth (PAYEMS > 150000 monthly additions) supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS > 150000, the S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

failure_condition: When PAYEMS > 150000 and UNRATE < 3.5%, the S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of such periods, or the Rank IC over any 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
